passages.english: Wives, in the same way, submit yourselves to your husbands, so that even if they refuse to believe the word, they will be won over without words by the behavior of their wives when they see your pure and reverent demeanor.

lines.text: Wives, in the same way, submit to your husbands.
Some husbands refuse to believe God's word.
But your behavior can win over your husband, even without speaking a word.
They will see your pure and reverent life.

passages.english: Your beauty should not come from outward adornment, such as braided hair or gold jewelry or fine clothes, but from the inner disposition of your heart, the unfading beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is precious in God’s sight.

lines.text: Your beauty should not come from outward things.
Your beauty is not braided hair, gold jewelry, or fine clothes.
Instead, your true beauty comes from within your heart.
Your true beauty is the unfading beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit.
This beauty is precious in God's sight.

passages.english: For this is how the holy women of the past adorned themselves. They put their hope in God and were submissive to their husbands, just as Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him lord. And you are her children if you do what is right and refuse to give way to fear.

lines.text: This is how the holy women of old made themselves beautiful.
They put their hope in God.
And they submitted to their husbands.
Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him lord.
You are children of Sarah — those who do good.
So do not give way to fear.

passages.english: Husbands, in the same way, treat your wives with consideration as a delicate vessel, and with honor as fellow heirs of the gracious gift of life, so that your prayers will not be hindered.

lines.text: Husbands, in the same way, treat your wives with understanding.
Your wife is the more delicate vessel.
So honor your wife.
Your wife is a fellow heir with you of the gracious gift of life.
Then your prayers will not be hindered.

passages.english: Finally, all of you, be like-minded and sympathetic, love as brothers, be tenderhearted and humble.

lines.text: Finally, all of you, be like-minded.
Be sympathetic to one another.
Love one another as brothers and sisters.
Be tenderhearted.
And be humble.

passages.english: Do not repay evil with evil or insult with insult, but with blessing, because to this you were called so that you may inherit a blessing.

lines.text: Do not repay evil with evil.
Do not repay insult with insult.
God has called you to bless others.
So, respond with blessing.
And then you will inherit a blessing.

passages.english: For, “Whoever would love life and see good days must keep his tongue from evil and his lips from deceitful speech.

lines.text: Suppose you want to love life and see good days.
Then keep your tongue from evil.
And keep your lips from deceitful speech.

passages.english: He must turn from evil and do good; he must seek peace and pursue it.

lines.text: Turn away from evil.
And do good.
Seek peace.
And pursue peace, so you may love life and see good days.

passages.english: For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and His ears are inclined to their prayer. But the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.”

lines.text: For the Lord's eyes are on the righteous.
And the Lord's ears are open to the prayers of the righteous.
But the Lord's face is against those who do evil.

passages.english: Who can harm you if you are zealous for what is good?

lines.text: Suppose you are eager to do what is good.
Then who can harm you?

passages.english: But even if you should suffer for what is right, you are blessed. “Do not fear what they fear; do not be shaken.”

lines.text: Suppose you do what is right.
But suppose you suffer — for doing right.
Then you are blessed.
“Do not fear what they fear.”
“Do not be shaken.”

passages.english: But in your hearts sanctify Christ as Lord. Always be prepared to give a defense to everyone who asks you the reason for the hope that is in you. But respond with gentleness and respect, keeping a clear conscience, so that those who slander you may be put to shame by your good behavior in Christ.

lines.text: But in your hearts, honor Christ as Lord.
Always be ready to give an answer.
Anyone may ask you the reason for the hope in you.
But answer with gentleness.
And answer with respect.
Keep a clear conscience.
Then those who slander you will be put to shame by your good life in Christ.

passages.english: For it is better, if it is God’s will, to suffer for doing good than for doing evil.

lines.text: Suppose it is God's will for you to suffer.
It is better to suffer for doing good.
It is worse to suffer for doing evil.

passages.english: For Christ also suffered for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God. He was put to death in the body but made alive in the Spirit, in whom He also went and preached to the spirits in prison who disobeyed long ago when God waited patiently in the days of Noah while the ark was being built. In the ark a few people, only eight souls, were saved through water.

lines.text: For Christ also suffered for sins, once for all.
Christ was righteous, yet He suffered for the unrighteous.
He suffered to bring you to God.
Christ was put to death in the body.
But God made Christ alive in the Spirit.
In the Spirit, Christ went and preached to the spirits in prison.
These spirits had disobeyed long ago.
This was in the days of Noah, when God waited patiently for people to turn back to Him.
At that time, the ark was being built.
Inside the ark, only eight people were saved through water.

passages.english: And this water symbolizes the baptism that now saves you also—not the removal of dirt from the body, but the pledge of a clear conscience toward God—through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, who has gone into heaven and is at the right hand of God, with angels, authorities, and powers subject to Him.

lines.text: The flood waters at the time of Noah point to baptism.
As the ark saved Noah and his family through the flood, so baptism now saves you too.
But baptism is not about washing dirt from your body.
Instead, baptism is the pledge of a clear conscience toward God.
Baptism saves you through the resurrection of Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ has gone into heaven.
Jesus Christ is at the right hand of God.
Angels, authorities, and powers are all subject to Jesus Christ.
